title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ohiopyle, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ohiopyle, PA
metaDescription: Ohiopyle, Fayette County mineral rights owner? We buy oil and gas interests near the Youghiogheny gorge, cash offers built on real activity, not pressure.
heroLead: Ohiopyle is best known for the Youghiogheny River gorge and the state park that draws visitors year-round, but the ridges and farmland around it in Fayette County sit on the southern flank of the Marcellus wet-gas play, and mineral ownership here often runs deeper than most people realize.
intro: Fayette County has a complicated ownership history because so much of it was coal country first — a lot of families here severed their coal rights generations ago while holding onto oil and gas, or vice versa, and untangling which rights you actually still hold near Ohiopyle can take real title work. We've done that work for other Fayette County families and don't charge you to sort it out.

sections.heading: Coal-and-Gas Split History in Fayette County
paragraphs: It's common around Ohiopyle for a deed to reference a coal severance from the early 1900s that has nothing to do with your current oil and gas rights, which confuses owners who assume 'mineral rights' were sold off long ago when really only the coal was. We read the full recorded chain of title, going back as far as needed, to confirm what you actually hold today before quoting anything.

Because this is the southern edge of the wet-gas fairway, activity has generally been less dense here than in core Washington or Greene County, which means valuation depends more heavily on whether your specific tract sits near an active unit than it would in a more heavily drilled part of the state.

sections.heading: What to Expect From an Offer
paragraphs: If your interest is unleased and sits outside current unit boundaries, our offer will reflect that lower near-term activity honestly rather than promising more than the ground supports. If you're already under lease with royalty history, we'll price against that history and current market terms, always as a range tied to activity rather than a flat guaranteed number.

faqs.question: My deed mentions a coal reservation from decades ago. Does that affect my gas rights?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Coal, oil, and gas were often severed separately in Fayette County, so a coal reservation doesn't automatically mean your oil and gas rights were also sold.

faqs.question: Is land near Ohiopyle State Park treated differently for mineral rights?
faqs.answer: State park boundaries don't change private mineral ownership outside the park, though development near park land can face additional local review that affects timing.

faqs.question: How long does a title review take before I get an offer?
faqs.answer: Usually a few days once we have your deed information, longer if the chain of title requires digging through older coal and gas severances.
